description:
The ULTIMATE ice cream Stabilizer video is here!

What they do, how much to use, how to heat them, for how long and more...

⸻

Ever had your homemade ice cream turn icy, gummy, or thin after a few days? In this video, I’ll show you exactly how to use stabilizers properly — the right way to hydrate, disperse, and blend them for silky-smooth, professional results.

You’ll learn:
✅ How stabilizers like guar, locust bean, and xanthan gum actually work
✅ The correct hydration temperatures and mixing steps
✅ How to avoid clumping and over-thickening
✅ The secret to perfectly smooth, scoopable texture that lasts

Whether you’re a home ice cream maker or a professional gelato producer, mastering stabilizers will take your frozen desserts to the next level.

⸻

🕒 Chapters / Timestamps

0:00 – Intro: Why stabilizers matter, general info
3:42 – Guar Gum
5:02 – Xanthan Gum
5:22 – Locust Bean Gum (LBG)
6:20 – Carrageenans (Kappa and Lambda)
7:40 – Carboxymethylcellulose (CMC)
8:53 – Tara Gum
9:51 – Sodium Alginate
10:50 – Gelatin
11:50 – Agar (Agar Agar)
13:00 – Pectin
13:51 – Konjac Gum
14:46 – Combining
17:35 – Aging, Outro and final thoughts

⸻

📊 Reference Chart

The reference chart is available on my Patreon Page here: https://www.patreon.com/c/PolarIceCreamery

⸻

🧂 Featured Stabilizers

Guar Gum • Locust Bean Gum • Xanthan Gum • Carrageenan • CMC • Tara Gum • Pectin • Gelatin • Agar

⸻

🔍 Keywords / SEO Tags

ice cream stabilizers, ice cream science, guar gum, xanthan gum, locust bean gum, how to use stabilizers, creamy ice cream, ice cream tutorial, artisan ice cream, homemade gelato, ice cream texture, professional ice cream making, ice cream base recipe, food science, Waka Tere

⸻

comments.text: Nick such a useful video and the chart just what a newbie to ice cream making like me needs. I do have a question though. I have just looked at the 'Specialingredients' (other makes are available) ice cream stabilizer I use and noticed when looking at the ingredients it includes Guar Gum and Agar Agar amongst others. Given that Guar gum is cold pressed and should not be taken above 50C for a short period of time and Agar Agar needs a much higher temperature for ages. How does that not negate what one or the other is meant to do? I always when using the stabilizer mix mentioned heat to 85C then immedieatley take it off the heat.

comments.text:
Nick - you used the jargon “clean label” a couple of times without explaining it or it’s significance. 
Also maybe worth flagging up that ALL these are veggie/vegan EXCEPT Gelatin. 
In jams and jellies, pectin needs acid to gel. Is that the same in this usage? (Would explain “good with fruits”…) 
And perhaps worth noting that even a crude sous vide setup (like the Instant Pot sv function) is great for ice cream base hydration heating control - with the side benefit that there is zero evaporation loss to be considered. 
Thanks for “bringing it all together”
comments.author: @dougal6569

comments.text:
Yeah the sous vide is an excellent way to manage evaporation. I don’t really care about “clean label” stuff but some do. I’ll maybe discuss it briefly in another video. Agar is usually considers the “vegan” gelatin as far as I’m aware. 
The big “issue” with sous vide is almost all recipes benefit from 1-2% evaporation. You can just increase milk powder slightly to negate that “issue” if you want to call it that.
